Waimakariri Mayor Dan Gordon, MP for Waimakariri Hon. Matt Doocey, and Chair of the Kaiapoi-Tuahiwi Community Board, Jackie Watson, had the honour of cutting the ribbon, joined by invited guests including Waimakariri District Councillors, Community Board members, staff, tenants, contractors and key partners.

Mayor Dan Gordon said for more than 65 years, Waimakariri District Council has supported older residents through our Housing for the Elderly service 🏘️

"This development at Courtenay Drive is a clear example of what can be achieved when local and central government, funders, and delivery partners work together with a shared purpose. 

"We are especially grateful to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development and the Rātā Foundation for their support, which helped unlock this former red zone land and turn it into a place of wellbeing and opportunity."

Thanks were also extended to the Taumata from Ngāi Tūāhuriri Rūnanga for their karakia and presence at the ceremony. 

Six tenants have now moved into their new units with 11 more set to pick up their keys next week 🔑

"To the new residents who will soon move in—welcome. This is your home and your community, and we hope it brings you comfort, connection, and a real sense of belonging," said Mayor Gordon. Located just inside the rear entrance of Ruataniwha Civic Centre / Kaiapoi Library, the new unit supports safer battery recycling and helps reduce the fire risks batteries can pose when they’re placed in kerbside rubbish bins or bags.

Over the past two years, four battery-related fires have been recorded within Waimakariri’s kerbside collection service and waste facilities — including one in a collection truck, putting the driver directly at risk.

The new recycling unit, provided by Phoenix Recycling Group, includes an internal fire suppression system and remote temperature monitoring. Residents can drop off unwanted and undamaged household batteries for free, from button cells through to power hand-tool batteries.

Car batteries, large batteries, damaged or leaking batteries, and other hazardous waste still need to be taken to the appropriate recycling area at Southbrook or Oxford Transfer Stations.

The funding announcement represents the next major step towards delivering one of the Waimakariri district’s most strategically important transport projects.

The REL has long been identified as critical infrastructure to support:
• Growth on Rangiora’s eastern side
• Improved transport efficiency and network resilience
• Reduced congestion through Southbrook
• Safer and more reliable travel connections across the district

Detailed design and property acquisition are expected to total $8.8 million, with NZTA contributing $4.5 m (or 51%) of the funding.

The project has also been recognised by the New Zealand Infrastructure Commission, Te Waihanga, as a national infrastructure priority due to its wider regional significance.

Mayor Dan Gordon says today’s announcement is a landmark moment for the district and an important signal of confidence in Waimakariri’s future growth.

Southbrook Road currently carries approximately 23,000 vehicle movements per day, with volumes continuing to increase alongside residential and business development.

          <p class="break-words text-color-text" data-test-id="about-us__description">
              When you get over 300 qualified, friendly and dedicated people together whose main focus is a community stretching over 225,000 hectares, from the Pacific Ocean to the Southern Alps, from the Waimakariri River to Hurunui, you can be sure that some good things are going to happen. That’s how it is with the Waimakariri District Council.

A lot of the work we do is unseen – sometimes literally. Sewerage, water reticulation, community support … it’s not normally the sort of stuff that commands news headlines and lead TV stories. But it does need to be done and, if it goes wrong, it also needs to be fixed. Who fixes the pothole in your street? Who mows the grass in your local park? Who arranges for your rubbish to be collected? Who keeps public swimming pools open and clean? Who puts books in the libraries? Who plans for future community needs? … the Council. We also assume some responsibility for maintaining a considerate, respectable and peaceable community – the regulatory side of Council activities.

What we like best is when people talk to us about their needs, wants and aspirations for themselves and their community, about their issues and problems – that gives us the opportunity to act on them and help to satisfy the needs or resolve the issues.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Today marked the official opening of our housing for the elderly units at Courtenay Drive, Kaiapoi 🎀✂️

Waimakariri Mayor Dan Gordon, MP for Waimakariri Hon. Matt Doocey, and Chair of the Kaiapoi-Tuahiwi Community Board, Jackie Watson, had the honour of cutting the ribbon, joined by invited guests including Waimakariri District Councillors, Community Board members, staff, tenants, contractors and key partners.

Mayor Dan Gordon said for more than 65 years, Waimakariri District Council has supported older residents through our Housing for the Elderly service 🏘️

"This development at Courtenay Drive is a clear example of what can be achieved when local and central government, funders, and delivery partners work together with a shared purpose. 

"We are especially grateful to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development and the Rātā Foundation for their support, which helped unlock this former red zone land and turn it into a place of wellbeing and opportunity."

Thanks were also extended to the Taumata from Ngāi Tūāhuriri Rūnanga for their karakia and presence at the ceremony. 

Six tenants have now moved into their new units with 11 more set to pick up their keys next week 🔑

"To the new residents who will soon move in—welcome. This is your home and your community, and we hope it brings you comfort, connection, and a real sense of belonging," said Mayor Gordon. </p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">A new battery drop-off point is now available in Kaiapoi, helping make it easier for residents to safely dispose of used household batteries.

Located just inside the rear entrance of Ruataniwha Civic Centre / Kaiapoi Library, the new unit supports safer battery recycling and helps reduce the fire risks batteries can pose when they’re placed in kerbside rubbish bins or bags.

Over the past two years, four battery-related fires have been recorded within Waimakariri’s kerbside collection service and waste facilities — including one in a collection truck, putting the driver directly at risk.

The new recycling unit, provided by Phoenix Recycling Group, includes an internal fire suppression system and remote temperature monitoring. Residents can drop off unwanted and undamaged household batteries for free, from button cells through to power hand-tool batteries.

Car batteries, large batteries, damaged or leaking batteries, and other hazardous waste still need to be taken to the appropriate recycling area at Southbrook or Oxford Transfer Stations.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Waimakariri District Council has agreed on a 4.99% average rates increase as part of its Annual Plan — one of the lowest in Canterbury!

Importantly, that figure includes Three Waters costs. 

Excluding Three Waters, the average general rates increase for most households is around 2.9%.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">A significant milestone for the Rangiora Eastern Link (REL) project was confirmed today, with NZ Transport Agency (NZTA) approving co-funding for detailed design and property acquisition.

  <div class="attributed-text-segment-list__container relative mt-1 mb-1.5 babybear:mt-0 babybear:mb-0.5">
    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="feed-reshare-content__commentary">In Kaiapoi, just north of Christchurch, we're busy wrapping Kaiapoi River Bridge's columns in carbon fibre.

To build the new Belfast to Pegasus Motorway we need to strengthen Kaiapoi River Bridge on State Highway 1. We’re going to be adding another southbound lane to the bridge, so it needs to be strong enough to carry the increased number of people travelling over it.

The Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass is a Road of National Significance that’ll create an efficient and reliable connection between Belfast and Pegasus, while supporting economic growth and making travel through Woodend safer.

People travelling can’t see this from the road but, behind the scenes – or maybe beneath the scenes in this case – workers are repairing the concrete in the columns and then wrapping the top and bottom of each column in the black carbon fibre you see in the photo below.

Carbon fibre is an extremely strong material. Concrete columns expand outward when they have weight put on them – this makes them weaken over time. Wrapping the columns in carbon fibre restricts this expansion and, because it’s a strong material, helps the columns support more weight. That means we can add more weight to the bridge (with the extra lane and more people travelling) without needing to build a new structure. 

We’re also painting the columns with anti-graffiti and ultraviolet light-resistant paint.

While that’s happening to the bridge’s support columns, we’re also strengthening the bridge’s beams above the abutments (the sections that connect the bridge to the land). We’re adding reinforced concrete around the existing beams to make them wider and deeper. These’ll reduce how much the beams move during a large earthquake.

Together, our improvements will make the bridge more resilient in an earthquake, helping to limit damage.

You can keep up to date with our work by following this page and subscribing to our newsletter: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/gj6d3em8?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/gj6d3em8</a></p>
